name: Nation of Ulysses
label: Dischord
lede: Not a band, they insisted, but a political party: five DC kids with a manifesto, a trumpet, and a plan to secede from rock and roll.

eras.title: Ulysses, then a nation
eras.text: In a DC scene that had spent the '80s arguing about sincerity, a group of teenagers showed up talking like a revolutionary cell. They started as a quartet called Ulysses; adding Tim Green on second guitar turned them into The Nation of Ulysses.

years.h: Ulysses, the quartet before the Nation
years.p: Ulysses is [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]] on vocals and trumpet, Steve Kroner on guitar, Steve Gamboa on bass and [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] on drums. Canty is the younger brother of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] drummer [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]].

years.h: [[Tim Green|19b6bda7-fbb1-4a45-a3c7-687114167e8c]] joins; Ulysses becomes The Nation of Ulysses
years.p: Tim Green comes in as Ulysses' second guitarist, and the band takes a new name to match the ambition: The Nation of Ulysses.

eras.title: The sassiest boy in America
eras.text: Before they'd released a note, Nation of Ulysses had a doctrine. The zine Ulysses Speaks mixed '60s radicals, French Situationists and juvenile delinquency into what they called the Ulysses Aesthetic, handed out at shows and sent by mail over nine issues.

years.h: The Ulysses Speaks zine
years.p: Ian Svenonius writes most of Nation of Ulysses' zine, and Tim Green helps with layout. Dischord's bio describes the band the way the zine did: a violent separatist political party operating out of Washington.

years.cap: The Nation of Ulysses, circa 1989–92 · Wikimedia
q: To create a space of liberation where anything's possible.
years.h: Sassy names Ian Svenonius its first Sassiest Boy in America
years.p: The teen magazine picks the Nation of Ulysses singer before the band has an official record out. Svenonius uses the space to call rock a corrupt medium.
years.xp: It was a perfect collision: a glossy magazine for teenage girls and a singer who talked like a pamphlet. Svenonius told Sassy the band wanted a space where anything was possible and dismissed traditional rock groups outright.

eras.title: Thirteen points
eras.text: The records finally came, fast and wiry and full of slogans, with song titles that read like party platform planks. Live, it was closer to a riot than a recital.

years.h: Nation of Ulysses' first 7" · Dischord No. 46.5
years.p: Three songs, later added as bonus tracks on the 13 Point Program to Destroy America CD.

years.h: 13 Point Program to Destroy America · Dischord No. 57
years.p: Nation of Ulysses' debut album, recorded at Inner Ear in January with [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] of [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]] and Ian MacKaye. Sixteen tracks, among them Look Out! Soul Is Back, Hot Chocolate City and You're My Miss Washington, D.C.
play: A Kid Who Tells On Another Kid is a Dead Kid

years.h: Nation of Ulysses shows that drew blood
years.p: Ian Svenonius described Nation of Ulysses shows as masochistic, cacophonous and violent. He broke his arm, his leg and his head at various points along the way.

years.h: The Birth of the Ulysses Aesthetic 7" · Dischord No. 62
years.p: Three more Nation of Ulysses songs with Eli Janney producing, subtitled the synthesis of speed and transformation.

years.h: Live at Oz Nightclub, Seattle, August 26, 1991
yt: Live at Oz Nightclub, Seattle, August 26, 1991

eras.title: Plays pretty, then the nation dissolves
eras.text: Plays Pretty for Baby was sharper and stranger, with more soul and more jazz in it. Then Nirvana happened, the ground moved, and in fall 1992 Nation of Ulysses broke up.

years.h: Nation of Ulysses record in Memphis with Primal Scream
years.p: On tour with [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]], Nation of Ulysses find their Memphis show was never promoted. They flyer the streets, run into [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]], and play the Antenna Club to five people, two of them from Primal Scream.
years.xp:
Primal Scream were in Memphis making a record and invited Nation of Ulysses to their studio. The band cut five songs in nine hours, on Primal Scream's dime: the Memphis Demos, including N-Sub Ulysses, Shakedown and Mockingbird, Yeah.

Several of those songs are the ones that anchor Plays Pretty for Baby.

years.h: Plays Pretty for Baby · Dischord No. 71
years.p: Nation of Ulysses' second album, produced by Ian MacKaye at Inner Ear. The Kingdom of Heaven Must Be Taken By Storm, The Sound of Jazz To Come, Presidents of Vice: the titles alone are a manifesto.

years.h: Steve Kroner leaves Nation of Ulysses mid-album
years.p: Guitarist Steve Kroner leaves during the recording of the band's third album. Ian Svenonius, Tim Green, Steve Gamboa and James Canty keep going.

q: The epoch changed with the advent of digital music and the Nirvana explosion.
years.h: Nation of Ulysses break up
years.p: Nation of Ulysses break up. Ian Svenonius, James Canty and Steve Gamboa start the short-lived Cupid Car Club.
years.xp:
Svenonius has blamed the timing, not the members: digital music was arriving, Nirvana had cracked the underground open, and what came next was indie rock, which he called a vacuous form.

Guitarist Steve Kroner was already gone. The last songs sat on four-track tape until Dischord released them as The Embassy Tapes in 2000.

years.h: Live at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, 1992
yt: Live at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, 1992

eras.title: The party in exile
eras.text: Nation of Ulysses never reformed, but its members never stopped. Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa carried on together in The Make-Up, Green became a producer, and the final tapes finally came out.

years.h: Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa form [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]]
years.p: Ian Svenonius, James Canty and Steve Gamboa's post-Ulysses group runs until 2001. Ex-Nation of Ulysses guitarist Tim Green goes on to engineer and produce, and to play in [[The Fucking Champs|e786319e-c2df-4409-8e92-55fac38b5841]].

years.h: The Embassy Tapes · Dischord No. 124
years.p: Nation of Ulysses' last songs, recorded as a four-piece with Ian MacKaye at The Embassy in September 1992, sat on four-track tape until Dischord released them in 2000.
years.xp: Guitarist Steve Kroner had already left during the recording of what would have been the band's third album. These half-inch four-track tapes are the sound of that album, never finished.

years.h: Ian Svenonius starts [[Weird War|f6fb557c-2f0f-4d17-97d9-13371fbe0ea6]]
years.p: Weird War is one of several Ian Svenonius bands after The Make-Up, with Chain and the Gang and Escape-ism later on.

years.h: Ian Svenonius's first book, The Psychic Soviet
years.p: Ian Svenonius's first book of essays carries the voice of the Nation of Ulysses zine Ulysses Speaks into hard covers.

years.h: Ian Svenonius hosts Soft Focus
years.p: Ian Svenonius hosts the interview show Soft Focus on VBS.tv through 2010, talking to artists in places as grand as the Guggenheim.

years.h: Ian Svenonius's rock-band how-to book
years.p: Ian Svenonius publishes Supernatural Strategies for Making a Rock 'n' Roll Group, a how-to guide from the Nation of Ulysses singer who spent 1990 trying to destroy rock and roll.
